rules.statement: In a test project, when the code under test is expected to make exactly one call or produce exactly one item, assert the exact count (for example `Assert.Single`) instead of only checking that the collection is non-empty.
rules.why: A loosened `Assert.NotEmpty` lets a duplicated or extra call pass the test unnoticed.
rules.check: Look for tests that replaced `Assert.Single` or an exact-count assertion with `Assert.NotEmpty` or a `>= 1` check, where the expected count is actually one and no comment explains why more are allowed.

rules.statement: When two handlers repeat the same guard logic, such as reading a feature, null-checking it and returning the same problem result, move it into one private helper that both call.
rules.why: Separate copies of a fail-closed check can drift apart when the rule changes.
rules.check: Look for the same feature lookup, null check and early-return error result copied across sibling handler methods in the diff.

rules.statement: Don't report calling `IHttpMessageHandlerFactory.CreateHandler` and wrapping the result in a new `HttpMessageInvoker` on each request as a per-request handler allocation, and don't ask for the invoker to be cached.
rules.why: `CreateHandler` returns the cached handler of the name's active entry, so the only per-request cost is a small invoker that disposes nothing. Caching the invoker would break the handler rotation the factory owns.
rules.check: Before reporting, confirm the handler comes from `IHttpMessageHandlerFactory` and the invoker is created with `disposeHandler: false` or doesn't own the handler. Also look for tests that require the factory to be asked on every request.

rules.statement: When a change narrows or moves what a type sets up, rename the type and update its doc comment so both describe what it does now.
rules.why: A stale name or summary sends readers looking for setup the class no longer owns.
rules.check: Look for classes whose body was reduced or moved to a base class in the diff while the class name and `<summary>` still describe the old responsibilities.

rules.statement: Don't report a mechanical conversion in a file as unrelated churn when the pull request description says it covers that kind of conversion and the file's history shows the file falls within that scope.
rules.why: Such a change is in scope by design, so the finding is a false positive.
rules.check: Before reporting out-of-scope churn, read the pull request description and check which earlier commits or pull requests touched the file.
